name: Hairfryer (VST3) (in development)
description: A free Windows VST3 vocal strip that attempts to convert a clean, loud singing voice into a metal-ish one — growls, gutturals, pig squeals, fry based on physics. No AI and no voice model: it splits the voice into glottal source and vocal tract in real time, wrecks only the source with a genuine chaotic map locked to your glottal pulses plus a self-oscillating false-fold resonator, and puts your own vowels back on top. The melody survives, the words survive, the voice is a monster — right now it distorts the voice in weird ways, and I don't know if it is useful to make a "metallize" VST3 for voice. It's fun to try, because it is probably impossible to do. It also has gate, de-esser, EQ, tube heat, compressor and limiter like any other vocal strip :)
note: Windows VST3 · build 260826.1 · free download · 9-page manual & cookbook included.
